primitives.name: Confirmatory Factor Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: The CFA finds that offensive Four Factors are indicators of a single latent factor, labeled "offensive quality." The "defensive quality" latent factor is estimable when replacing opposing teams' free throw rate with steals per possession.
primitives.assumptions: The hypothesized factor structure is correct, errors are uncorrelated across indicators, and the covariance matrix is positive definite.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model mis-specification (e.g., omitted factors) causes underfitting, while over-parameterization leads to Heywood cases and non-convergence.

reasoning_traces.think:
SEM provides a rigorous framework to test whether multiple observed 'Four Factors' (e.g., effective field goal percentage, turnover rate) are manifestations of a single underlying latent construct (offensive quality). This is achieved through Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), which imposes a priori constraints on the factor loadings. Once the latent factors are extracted, Path Modeling allows us to specify direct and indirect relationships between these constructs and outcomes (winning percentage) while controlling for covariates (team salary). The key advantage is that SEM accounts for measurement error in the latent variables, leading to unbiased estimates of the structural relationships compared to traditional OLS regression on raw factor scores.
